digest.component_or_area: Jira reconciler — inbound link differing and apply layer
propositions: Inbound link differ is ADD-only by design and docstring (lines 380, 396), never emitting removals when Jira link is deleted, creating asymmetry with outbound direction which has a removal path via _diff_link_removals
Link deleted on Jira peer is never removed from local rebar ticket because apply layer silently discards non-add records (apply_inbound_records.py:560–562 drops any action != 'add')
Local-wins semantics: peer-deleted links are re-added on next pass rather than mirrored, convergent but divergent from strict mirroring and leaves local data intact

Arbitration between directions requires distinguishing brand-new unmanaged local links (never pushed) from managed links the peer actually deleted, but managed_refs alone cannot make that distinction — both states are identical on all observable inputs

Guards G1–G5 establish when removal is safe: observed enrichment, bound target, managed ref, precedence rule, and relation matching; G1 specifically requires issuelinks key presence to avoid data loss on failed enrichment

Ecosystem research shows link deletion mirroring is not commonly handled and is deliberately declined by comparable tools (Aha!, Asana–Jira, Workfront–Jira) citing data-loss risk; this is not a parity gap with Cloud
